title: Strict constant-complex comparison interfaces
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, I an ideal, g:X→Y a scheme morphism, A_n=R/I^(n+1), B_W=lim_n underline(A_n)_W, and use the finite quotient complexes D_W,n and reduction data of [def-a1-constant-complex-quotient-model]. All module inverse images and exact derived factorizations use [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; local inverse sections use [def-sfb-proetale-inverse-image-unit-section] and the inverse-image module/tensor interfaces [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison]. Define the Roos arrow as 1 minus the shift induced by consecutive reduction transitions, and its target cone as Cone(1-shift)[-1] [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. A RoosAugmentation is a chain map from each bounded finite-projective completed constant complex into this cone. It is normalized when its product projection is the prescribed reduction product map, its shifted-product component is zero, the product map kills the Roos arrow, and it is natural in scalar chain maps. A FiniteComparison consists of natural isomorphisms g_n^*D_Y,n≅D_X,n, natural pulled consecutive transitions after restriction to underline(R)_X, and an isomorphism of the resulting strict towers. Its normalization sends pulled constant tensors a⊗p to a⊗p, sends the pullback of every source transition section to that transition's pulled section, and has the prescribed restricted level components. Localizing a level isomorphism gives FiniteComparison.derived via the exact pullback factorization. For any coefficient map c:g^(-1)B_Y→B_X define completedPullback as geometric module inverse image followed by sheaf scalar extension along c, and completedPullbackComplex termwise when additive. Define scaledPulledSection as the target scalar multiple of the actual pulled section. A GeometricReduction consists of c, additivity, isomorphisms from pulled completed constant complexes to the target completed complex, and maps from those pulled complexes to the restricted pulled finite levels. Its normalization requires the limit projection equations for c, the balanced formula b'⊗inverse(b⊗p)↦b'c(unit(b))⊗p, the pulled reduction formula pr_n(b')·pull(alpha_n(m)), commutation of the reduction square with the finite level comparison and target alpha_n, and naturality in scalar chain maps. No inverse to c is part of the data.
